name: patient_view_own_access_log_floor
rationale: The specification explicitly grants patients the ability to view their own access log. This floor prevents synthesis from satisfying the policy set with no permission for this required patient self-access workflow, and uses the schema's patient-specific ownership hook rather than relying only on principal type.
plain_english_summary: A patient should be permitted to view an access log when the log is for that same patient and the request context also identifies that patient.
source_excerpt: A patient can view their own access log; sentence 197: The patient views their access log for themself or a represented person.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewAccessLog", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && context.patient == principal && resource.patient == principal };

alternatives_considered.label: role_only_patient_access_log
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Permit any Patient to view any AccessLog based only on the Patient principal type.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewAccessLog", resource) when { principal is Patient };

name: patient_view_access_log_own_ceiling
rationale: The approved floor permits a patient to view only their own access log, but the ownership boundary has not yet been safety-bounded. The specification says patients view their access log for themself or for a represented person, so a candidate policy must not allow Patient-principal access to unrelated patients' access logs through this own-record path.
plain_english_summary: A patient should be allowed to view an access log as a Patient only when the log is for that same patient and the active session belongs to that patient.
source_excerpt: A patient can view their own access log; sentence 197: The patient views their access log for themself or a represented person.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewAccessLog", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && context.patient == principal && resource.patient == principal };

examples_adversarial.description: A patient attempts to view another patient's access log while the request context names the other patient. This should not be permitted under the patient's own-access-log path.

alternatives_considered.label: role_only_patient_access_log_ceiling
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Allow any Patient principal to view any AccessLog based only on Patient type and active session.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewAccessLog", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal };

alternatives_considered.label: context_only_patient_access_log_ceiling
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Require the context patient to match the principal but do not require the AccessLog resource's patient to match, which would leave a resource ownership gap.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewAccessLog", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && context.patient == principal };

name: personal_representative_view_represented_access_log_floor
rationale: The approved access-log atoms cover only a patient's own access log. The specification also explicitly permits access-log viewing for a person for whom the requester is a personal representative. Because personal-representative status is patient-specific in both the prose and schema, the property must use the representedPatients relationship rather than relying on the PersonalRepresentative principal type alone.
plain_english_summary: A personal representative should be permitted to view an access log for a patient they represent when the active session belongs to that representative and the request context identifies the same patient as the log.
source_excerpt: A patient can view their own access log, or the access log for a person for whom they are a personal representative.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewAccessLog", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && context.patient in principal.representedPatients && resource.patient == context.patient };

examples_adversarial.description: A personal representative with an active session tries to view the access log for a patient included in their representedPatients set; a policy that only permits patients to view their own logs would incorrectly deny this required workflow.

alternatives_considered.label: role_only_personal_representative
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Permit any PersonalRepresentative to view any AccessLog based only on principal type.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewAccessLog", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal };

name: personal_representative_view_represented_access_log_ceiling
rationale: The approved floor permits a personal representative to view represented patients' access logs, but the same ownership/representation boundary also needs a safety ceiling so a candidate policy cannot permit representatives to view logs for patients they do not represent or with a mismatched request context.
plain_english_summary: A personal representative should be allowed to view an access log only when the active session belongs to that representative, the request context identifies a patient they represent, and the log is for that same represented patient.
source_excerpt: A patient can view their own access log, or the access log for a person for whom they are a personal representative.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewAccessLog", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && context.patient in principal.representedPatients && resource.patient == context.patient };

examples_adversarial.description: A personal representative tries to view an access log for a patient who is not in their representedPatients set, even though the session is active.

alternatives_considered.label: session_only_personal_representative_ceiling
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Allow any personal representative with an active session to view any access log. Rejected because personal representative status is patient-specific in the spec and schema.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewAccessLog", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal };

name: hcp_no_patient_credential_view_disjointness
rationale: The requirements explicitly state that an HCP must not view a patient's security question or password. The schema exposes a single viewCredential action over User resources, but it does not expose which credential field is being viewed, so the safe reviewable boundary is to exclude HCP credential viewing for Patient resources rather than pretending field-level password/security-question visibility can be distinguished.
plain_english_summary: An HCP must not be permitted to view credentials for a Patient user through the credential-viewing action.
source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password; sentence 76: The HCP does not have the ability to enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewCredential", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && !(resource is Patient) };

examples_adversarial.description: An HCP in their own active session attempts to view credential information for a Patient account. Because the schema lacks a field-level credential selector, this request must be treated as unsafe under the patient password/security-question prohibition.

alternatives_considered.label: field_specific_password_or_security_question_check
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Would distinguish viewing a password from viewing a security question or other credential metadata, matching the prose more precisely, but the schema has no context or resource attribute naming the requested credential field for viewCredential.

name: hcp_no_patient_password_or_security_question_view_disjointness
rationale: The specification explicitly says HCPs must not view a patient's password or security question. The schema now exposes the credential-field selector as context.credentialField, so this can be stated as a field-specific safety property rather than the previously rejected overbroad Patient credential proxy.
plain_english_summary: An HCP must not be permitted to view a Patient user's password or security question; any otherwise permitted HCP credential viewing must exclude those patient credential fields.
source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password; sentence 76: The HCP does not have the ability to enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewCredential", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && !(resource is Patient && (context.credentialField == "password" || context.credentialField == "securityQuestion")) };

name: hcp_patient_sensitive_credential_view_forbidden_disjointness
rationale: The specification explicitly prohibits HCPs from viewing a patient's password or security question. This repaired disjointness atom uses the schema's context.credentialField boundary to identify only the forbidden condition, without creating or implying any general HCP permission to view other credential fields or non-patient credentials.
plain_english_summary: An HCP must not be permitted to view a Patient user's password or security question.
source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password; sentence 76: The HCP does not have the ability to enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.
reference_cedar:
permit (principal is HCP, action == Action::"viewCredential", resource is User)
when { !(resource is Patient && (context.credentialField == "password" || context.credentialField == "securityQuestion")) };

examples_adversarial.description: An HCP attempts to view a Patient user's password through viewCredential. This must not be permitted regardless of whether other credential-viewing permissions exist elsewhere.
An HCP attempts to view a Patient user's security question through viewCredential. This must not be permitted by any otherwise applicable HCP credential-viewing rule.

alternatives_considered.label: safe_complement_as_general_hcp_credential_ceiling
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Encode the disjointness reference as a broad permit for HCP viewCredential whenever the target is not a Patient password or securityQuestion. Rejected because the negative source requirement does not grant HCPs permission to view other credential fields or non-patient credentials.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal is HCP, action == Action::"viewCredential", resource is User) when { !(resource is Patient && (context.credentialField == "password" || context.credentialField == "securityQuestion")) };

alternatives_considered.label: role_only_hcp_credential_denial
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Deny or exclude all HCP credential viewing regardless of the resource type or selected credential field. Rejected because the source requirement specifically names the patient's security question and password, not every possible credential-viewing request.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal is HCP, action == Action::"viewCredential", resource is User) when { false };

name: hcp_patient_sensitive_credential_view_forbidden_target_only_disjointness
rationale: The specification explicitly prohibits HCPs from viewing a patient's password or security question. This repaired disjointness atom identifies only the forbidden request slice using context.credentialField and a Patient resource target; it intentionally does not encode the complement as a positive permission for other credential fields or non-patient credentials.
plain_english_summary: No HCP permission may cover viewing a Patient user's password or security question.
source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password; sentence 76: The HCP does not have the ability to enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.
reference_cedar:
permit (principal is HCP, action == Action::"viewCredential", resource is User)
when { !(resource is Patient && (context.credentialField == "password" || context.credentialField == "securityQuestion")) };

examples_adversarial.description: An HCP attempts to view a Patient user's password through viewCredential. This request is in the forbidden target slice and must not be permitted by any HCP credential-viewing permission.

An HCP attempts to view a Patient user's security question through viewCredential. This request is in the forbidden target slice and must not be permitted, without implying anything about other credential fields.

alternatives_considered.label: broad_safe_complement_permit
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Permit HCP viewCredential whenever the resource is not a Patient password or securityQuestion. Rejected because the negative source requirement only forbids the sensitive patient credential slice and does not grant or characterize access to other credential fields or non-patient credentials.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal is HCP, action == Action::"viewCredential", resource is User) when { !(resource is Patient && (context.credentialField == "password" || context.credentialField == "securityQuestion")) };

alternatives_considered.label: forbid_policy_encoding
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Use a Cedar forbid policy for the forbidden slice. Rejected for this property-atom format because disjointness atoms are represented as target-only verifier constraints with a complete permit-form reference and an explicit disjoint_target_body.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: forbid (principal is HCP, action == Action::"viewCredential", resource is Patient) when { context.credentialField == "password" || context.credentialField == "securityQuestion" };

name: deactivated_patient_login_forbidden_disjointness
rationale: The specification explicitly states that a deactivated patient cannot log into the system. Because login is security-sensitive and the schema exposes the patient activation boundary as Patient.isActive, this safety boundary should be verified directly rather than relying only on role or session shape.
plain_english_summary: A deactivated patient must not be permitted to log into the system.
source_excerpt: A deactivated patient cannot be modified or log into the system, and can only be reactivated by an administrator.
reference_cedar:
permit (principal is Patient, action == Action::"login", resource is Session)
when { !(!principal.isActive) };

name: inactive_patient_login_forbidden_slice_disjointness
rationale: The specification explicitly states that a deactivated patient cannot log into the system, and the schema exposes that forbidden slice as Patient.isActive == false on the login principal. This replacement avoids interpreting the requirement as an affirmative permission for active patients to log in, because MID/password authentication is not represented in the login action context. The disjointness target is therefore the reviewable safety boundary: no Patient principal with isActive == false may be permitted for login.
plain_english_summary: A patient whose account is not active must not be permitted to log into the system; this property does not grant login permission to active patients.
source_excerpt: A deactivated patient cannot be modified or log into the system, and can only be reactivated by an administrator.
reference_cedar:
permit (principal is Patient, action == Action::"login", resource is Session)
when { !(!principal.isActive) };

examples_adversarial.description: A Patient principal with isActive == false attempts to log in. Even if another policy would otherwise allow Patient login, this forbidden slice must remain denied.

alternatives_considered.label: active_patient_login_complement
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Use the complement of the forbidden condition as a positive permit for active patients to log in.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal is Patient, action == Action::"login", resource is Session) when { principal.isActive };

alternatives_considered.label: forbid_inactive_patient_login
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Encode the negative requirement directly as a Cedar forbid policy. Rejected because Stage 2 disjointness atoms use a permit-shaped reference plus disjoint_target_body rather than forbid policies.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: forbid (principal is Patient, action == Action::"login", resource is Session) when { !principal.isActive };

rationale: The specification explicitly states that a deactivated patient cannot log into the system, and the schema exposes that forbidden slice as Patient.isActive == false on the login principal. This repaired disjointness atom avoids encoding the complement as an affirmative permit for active patients to log in, because the schema does not expose MID/password authentication in the login request. The reviewable requirement is only that no Patient principal with isActive == false may be permitted for login.

reference_cedar:
permit (principal is Patient, action == Action::"login", resource is Session)
when { !(!principal.isActive) };

examples_adversarial.description: A Patient principal with isActive == false attempts to log in. Even if another policy would otherwise allow Patient login, this forbidden slice must remain denied.

alternatives_considered.label: active_patient_login_complement
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Use the complement of the forbidden condition as a positive permit for active patients to log in. Rejected because the user explicitly requested not to imply an affirmative active-patient login permission, and MID/password authentication is not modeled in the schema.

alternatives_considered.label: double_negated_active_patient_complement
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Encode the disjointness reference as the safe complement of the forbidden slice. Rejected because it still reads as a positive permit for active patients to log in.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal is Patient, action == Action::"login", resource is Session) when { !(!principal.isActive) };

alternatives_considered.label: forbid_inactive_patient_login
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Encode the negative requirement directly as a Cedar forbid policy. Rejected because Stage 2 disjointness atoms are represented through disjoint_target_body rather than a forbid policy.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: forbid (principal is Patient, action == Action::"login", resource is Session) when { !principal.isActive };

name: patient_view_own_medical_record_floor
rationale: The specification explicitly grants patients access to their own medical records. This positive workflow is not covered by the already-approved access-log atoms, and it requires an explicit own-record equality rather than relying on the Patient principal type alone.
plain_english_summary: A patient should be permitted to view a medical record when the record is for that same patient, the request context identifies that same patient, and the active session belongs to the patient.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records ... for their own records and for patients they represent.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewMedicalRecord", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && context.patient == principal && resource.patient == principal };

examples_adversarial.description: A patient attempts to view another patient's medical record while using their own active session. The own-record equality should prevent treating Patient role membership alone as sufficient.

alternatives_considered.label: patient_role_only
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Permit any Patient principal to view any MedicalRecord based only on principal type and active session.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewMedicalRecord", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal };

name: patient_view_own_medical_record_ceiling
rationale: The approved floor permits a patient to view only their own medical record, using both resource.patient and context.patient as ownership boundaries. The prose frames access as for 'their own records', so a matching same-action safety ceiling is needed to prevent a candidate policy from also permitting patients to view other patients' medical records.
plain_english_summary: A patient should be allowed to view a medical record as a Patient only when the active session belongs to that patient, the request context identifies that same patient, and the medical record is for that same patient.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records ... for their own records and for patients they represent.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewMedicalRecord", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && context.patient == principal && resource.patient == principal };

examples_adversarial.description: A patient attempts to view another patient's medical record while using their own active session; the ownership boundary should prevent this over-permission.

alternatives_considered.label: session_only_patient_medical_record_ceiling
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Require only an active session for the patient principal and omit the resource.patient/context.patient ownership checks.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewMedicalRecord", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal };

alternatives_considered.label: resource_only_patient_medical_record_ceiling
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Check only resource.patient == principal and omit context.patient alignment, which would leave the request's patient context inconsistent with the viewed record.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewMedicalRecord", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && resource.patient == principal };

name: personal_representative_view_represented_medical_record_floor
rationale: The approved atoms cover patients viewing their own medical records, but the same source requirement also grants personal representatives access to medical records for patients they represent. This patient-specific representation relationship is an explicit boundary in the spec and is exposed by PersonalRepresentative.representedPatients, so it should be a separate floor atom rather than relying on role type alone.
plain_english_summary: A personal representative should be permitted to view a medical record for a patient they represent when the active session belongs to that representative and the request context identifies the same represented patient as the record.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records ... for their own records and for patients they represent.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewMedicalRecord", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && context.patient in principal.representedPatients && resource.patient == context.patient };

alternatives_considered.label: role_only_personal_representative_access
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Permit any PersonalRepresentative to view any MedicalRecord based only on principal type. Rejected because the spec says access is for patients they represent, and the schema exposes the patient-specific relationship.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewMedicalRecord", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal };

alternatives_considered.label: context_only_represented_patient
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Permit when the context names some patient without checking that the resource is for that same patient. Rejected because it would allow context/resource mismatch and fail to enforce the represented patient's record boundary.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewMedicalRecord", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && context.patient in principal.representedPatients };

name: personal_representative_view_represented_medical_record_ceiling
rationale: An approved floor permits personal representatives to view represented patients' medical records, but the same ownership/representation boundary is not yet covered by a same-action ceiling. The spec makes representation patient-specific, so a candidate policy must not permit a PersonalRepresentative to view medical records for patients they do not represent or where the request context does not match the record patient.

source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records ... for their own records and for patients they represent.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewMedicalRecord", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && context.patient in principal.representedPatients && resource.patient == context.patient };

examples_adversarial.description: A personal representative attempts to view a medical record for a patient not in their representedPatients set; a broad role-only policy would incorrectly permit it.

alternatives_considered.label: role_only_personal_representative_access
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Permit any PersonalRepresentative to view any MedicalRecord based only on role and active session.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewMedicalRecord", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal };

alternatives_considered.label: context_only_without_resource_match
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Require the context patient to be represented but do not require the MedicalRecord patient to match that context patient.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewMedicalRecord", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && context.patient in principal.representedPatients };

name: lhcp_view_patient_allowed_diagnostic_information_floor
rationale: The specification explicitly grants licensed health-care professionals access to diagnostic information when the patient has allowed that LHCP to view it. This floor prevents synthesis from satisfying only safety constraints while omitting the required approved-diagnostic-information workflow.
plain_english_summary: An LHCP should be permitted to view a patient's diagnostic information when the active session belongs to that LHCP, the request identifies the same patient as the diagnostic information, and the patient has included that LHCP in the diagnostic information's allowed viewers.
source_excerpt: Approved diagnostic information is diagnostic information that a patient allows a designated or other licensed health-care professional to view.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewDiagnosticInformation", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && context.patient == resource.patient && principal in resource.allowedViewers };

examples_adversarial.description: An LHCP who is explicitly listed in the diagnostic information's allowedViewers attempts to view that patient's diagnostic information using their own active session; a deny-only policy would incorrectly block this approved workflow.

alternatives_considered.label: role_only_lhcp_view
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Permit any LHCP to view diagnostic information based only on the LHCP principal type.

name: lhcp_view_patient_allowed_diagnostic_information_ceiling
rationale: The approved diagnostic-information floor permits LHCP viewing only when the patient/requested diagnostic information identifies the same patient and the LHCP is in the diagnostic information's allowedViewers set. The prose makes patient approval the boundary for approved diagnostic information, so a same-action ceiling is needed to prevent broader LHCP viewing of diagnostic information outside that allowed-viewer relationship.
plain_english_summary: An LHCP should be allowed to view a patient's diagnostic information only when the active session belongs to that LHCP, the request identifies the same patient as the diagnostic information, and that LHCP is included in the diagnostic information's allowed viewers.
source_excerpt: Approved diagnostic information is diagnostic information that a patient allows a designated or other licensed health-care professional to view.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewDiagnosticInformation", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && context.patient == resource.patient && principal in resource.allowedViewers };

examples_adversarial.description: An LHCP attempts to view diagnostic information for the patient named in the request, but the patient has not included that LHCP in the diagnostic information's allowed viewers.

alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Require only an active LHCP session and matching context/resource patient, omitting the patient-controlled allowedViewers relation.

name: patient_view_own_personal_health_information_floor
rationale: The specification explicitly grants patients access to personal health information for their own records. plain_english_summary: A patient should be permitted to view personal health information when it is for that same patient, the request context identifies that same patient, and the active session belongs to the patient.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records, family history, personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for patients they represent.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewPersonalHealthInformation", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && context.patient == principal && resource.patient == principal };

name: patient_view_own_personal_health_information_ceiling
rationale: The approved floor permits a patient to view only their own personal health information, with both the context patient and resource patient matching the principal. Because the source requirement uses an ownership boundary ('their own records'), a same-action ceiling is required so a candidate policy cannot also permit a Patient to view another patient's personal health information.
plain_english_summary: A patient should be allowed to view personal health information as a Patient only when the active session belongs to that patient, the request context identifies that same patient, and the personal health information is for that same patient.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view ... personal health information ... for their own records and for patients they represent.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewPersonalHealthInformation", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && context.patient == principal && resource.patient == principal };

examples_adversarial.description: A patient attempts to view another patient's personal health information by setting the request context to the other patient; the ownership boundary should block this even though the principal is a Patient.

alternatives_considered.label: principal_type_only_patient_view_phi
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Allow any Patient principal to view PersonalHealthInformation without requiring the resource and context patient to match the principal.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewPersonalHealthInformation", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal };

alternatives_considered.label: resource_only_patient_view_phi
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Require the resource to be for the principal but do not require the request context patient to match, leaving a mismatched-context path outside the reviewed boundary.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewPersonalHealthInformation", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && resource.patient == principal };

name: personal_representative_view_represented_personal_health_information_floor
rationale: The approved atoms cover a patient's own personal health information access, but the same source sentence also explicitly grants personal representatives access for patients they represent. plain_english_summary: A personal representative should be permitted to view personal health information for a patient they represent when the active session belongs to that representative and the request context identifies the same represented patient as the record.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records, family history, personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for patients they represent.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewPersonalHealthInformation", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session.user == principal && context.patient in principal.representedPatients && resource.patient == context.patient };

alternatives_considered.label: patient_only_access
